title: Protocol and Safehouse
premise: Ada Zhou, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Trust—an embassy that exists only in encrypted cables—learns that her own voiceprint has unlocked a server in Tallinn containing the Trust's darkest ledger. Ordered to extract a defector named Ilmar Kask who claims to hold the decryption key, Ada discovers Ilmar is bait, dangled by a Trust faction purging its own ghosts. As hunters close in across three countries, Ada realizes her carefully constructed identity was itself a Trust fabrication, built to keep a witness hidden: her. Choosing loyalty to the living over the institution that made her, Ada burns the ledger, trades her invisibility for Ilmar's freedom, and walks into an unclassified life—watched, but finally her own.
about_author: Edmund Lockridge is the pen name of a former policy analyst who spent a decade writing briefing books for institutions he cannot name. He lives near a port city and writes about people whose jobs require them to be forgettable.

chapters.title: Go-Bag Rules
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A routine night in Vienna: she cleans up a diplomat's indiscretion, checks her go-bag, and recites her cover story like a prayer. The beat is controlled competence masking loneliness—she knows no one who knows her real name.

chapters.title: The Voice That Wasn't Mine
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. A Trust handler alerts her that her voiceprint authenticated a server in Tallinn at 3:14 a.m.—while she slept. The emotional beat is vertigo: the first crack in her belief that she controls her own identity.

chapters.title: Kask
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, with an intercepted dossier in Ilmar's voice. In Tallinn, defector Ilmar Kask surfaces claiming he can open the same server. Ada is ordered to extract him. Beat: suspicion—his file is too clean, his timing too perfect.

chapters.title: Ferry to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The first meeting with Ilmar on a Baltic ferry; he recognizes her before she introduces herself. Beat: uncanny familiarity—he says her childhood street name, one that exists in no Trust file she's seen.

chapters.title: Safehouse Protocol
chapters.summary: Ilmar's POV. Inside a rural safehouse, Ilmar tests Ada's loyalties with half-truths, revealing he knew her mother. Beat: guarded tenderness—two liars circling the possibility of honesty.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ilmar shows her a fragment of the server's contents: names of people the Trust erased, including an entry labeled with a girl's photograph. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Vienna Rewinds
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Summoned home, Ada finds her apartment subtly rearranged—someone is rehearsing her life. Beat: paranoia made domestic; the lie she polished is being polished by others.

chapters.title: Handler's Hands
chapters.summary: Handler Voss's POV. Voss, Ada's superior, reports to an unnamed faction that the extraction is proceeding and the asset 'remains unaware.' Beat: cold institutional menace; the reader learns Ada is the operation's true target.

chapters.title: Run Through Riga
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilmar's alternating POV. A dead-drop goes wrong and they flee through Riga's old town under fire from men with Trust-grade equipment. Beat: forced partnership crystallizing into trust.

chapters.title: What Mother Left
chapters.summary: Ilmar's POV. Ilmar confesses: he was her mother's colleague, and the server holds her mother's testimony about the Trust's erasure program. Beat: grief and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confronts the evidence: Ilmar's defection was engineered to draw her out of cover. She must decide whether his warning is still true even if his arrival was staged. Beat: painful clarity—being used doesn't make the danger unreal.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours in Gdansk
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Holed up in a Gdansk shipyard flat, they plan to reach the server before the Trust's purge team deletes it. Beat: quiet resolve; Ada stops being an employee and becomes a protagonist.

chapters.title: Voss Calls
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, one-sided phone call. Voss offers her a clean life if she delivers Ilmar and forgets the ledger. Beat: temptation voiced gently—the corruption of power wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: The Second Safehouse
chapters.summary: Ilmar's POV. They shelter with an old network contact who betrays their location for a pension. Beat: the cost of belonging to institutions—everyone is someone's asset.

chapters.title: Interlude: The Girl in the Photograph
chapters.summary: Fragmented POV—Ada's recovered memory. A childhood night, her mother burning papers, a man with Voss's voice. Beat: memory as evidence; Ada's past reassembles against her will.

chapters.title: Tallinn Again
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilmar's alternating POV. They infiltrate the server site during a Trust facility rotation. Beat: rising tension—too easy, and both know it.

chapters.title: The Room Where She Was Made
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the archive, Ada finds her own file: recruited as a child, identity constructed, memory edited after her mother's death. Beat: the novel's emotional nadir—she was never hiding from the Trust; she was hidden by it.

chapters.title: Voss in the Flesh
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Voss arrives, not with killers but with an offer and a gun, explaining that the ledger must die so the Trust can survive. Beat: climax of ideology—power arguing it corrupts for good reasons.

chapters.title: Extraction, Inverted
chapters.summary: Ada and Ilmar's alternating POV. Ilmar sacrifices his escape to trigger the server's dead-man upload; Ada chooses to broadcast the ledger rather than bargain. Beat: climax of action and principle.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Snow
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The ledger is public; Voss is disavowed by the very faction he served; Ilmar, wounded, is evacuated by journalists, not spies. Beat: exhaustion and fragile victory.

chapters.title: A Name of Her Own
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada declines the Trust's final offer of a new cover, keeping the name Ada Zhou as hers by right of use, not assignment. Beat: reclamation of self.

chapters.title: Unlisted
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, months later. Living unclassified in a coastal town, she receives a postcard in her mother's cipher—someone from the old life survived. Beat: belonging earned, vigilance kept, story open but resolved.
